title: Lambdas, closures, and static lambdas
hook: On the 199-to-999 concurrent attempt-submit path, an innocent lambda that captures this pins the whole request graph until the Task completes.

sections.heading: Expression lambdas, statement lambdas, conversion
sections.prose: A lambda is an anonymous function: (parameters) => expression or a block. The compiler converts it to a delegate type (Action, Func, or a named delegate) or, when the target is Expression<TDelegate>, to an expression tree. Statement lambdas cannot become expression trees. Natural types let you assign var Increment = (int x) => x + 1. C# 12 added default parameter values on explicitly typed lambdas. C# 14 lets you write modifiers (ref, in, out, scoped, ref readonly) on implicitly typed parameters; params still requires a typed list.

snippets.label: C# 14 modifiers on a simple lambda
snippets.explanation: Before C# 14 this required (string text, out int id). The delegate type still supplies the types; the lambda no longer repeats them.

sections.heading: Closures, this, and static lambdas
sections.prose: A lambda that reads a local, a parameter, or instance state is rewritten as a display class. Capturing this (even by touching a field) keeps the enclosing object alive for as long as the delegate is reachable. static on a lambda or anonymous function forbids capture; the compiler errors if you touch instance members or outer locals. Use static on hot-path filters and on anything stored in a static event. Shared mutable captures across parallel Task.WhenAll submissions are data races, not clever reuse.

snippets.label: static lambda versus capturing the request
snippets.explanation: The factory marked static cannot close over payload. That is the point: you pass data through the cache API instead of accidentally pinning the worker.

interviewTakeaways: Lambdas convert to delegates or to Expression<T>; statement bodies cannot be trees.
Capture allocates a closure class; capturing this extends object lifetime.
static lambdas (C# 9) are the compiler-enforced no-capture form.
C# 14: parameter modifiers without repeating types; params still needs types.
commonPitfalls: Subscribing a capturing lambda to a static event and never unsubscribing.
Mutating a captured int from parallel attempt-submit tasks.
Expecting a statement lambda to be translated by an IQueryable provider.

jsTsCorrelations.concept: Closures and lexical this vs arrow functions
jsTsCorrelations.note: JS arrows capture lexical this. C# lambdas capture this only if you reference instance members; static forbids it. JS has no static lambda equivalent.
